1) BDNF overexpression in neural stem cells enhances their survival and differentiation in vitro, and their survival and trophic effects on host cholinergic neurons in vivo.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of neural stem cell lines as a tool for studying neural cell development and differentiation

the development of new strategies for the generation and characterization of neural stem cell lines, with the identification of new molecular markers for neural stem cells, and with the use of neural stem cell-based gene delivery systems to study the in vivo effects on neuronal survival, differentiation and function.
the development of novel strategies for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases, based on the use of genetically modified neural stem cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BDNF is a potent survival factor for neural stem cells, and that its overproduction may result in detrimental effects, especially in the adult brain.
BDNF overproduction in vivo, in the adult rat brain, is not a good strategy for neuroprotection and neuroregeneration.
BDNF over-expression is beneficial for the survival of neural stem cells and their progeny.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BDNF gene expression is a crucial factor in the in vitro and in vivo fate of CNS-derived neural progenitor cells.
BDNF is a key molecule in neural development and in the regulation of neuronal survival and differentiation.
BDNF is a key regulator of neural stem cell survival, proliferation and/or differentiation in vitro.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BDNF is not only a survival factor, but it is also a differentiation factor.
BDNF gene therapy is not a simple matter.
neural stem cells are a promising tool for gene therapy, and that BDNF gene delivery can be a powerful tool to enhance the therapeutic potential of stem cell therapy.
